spotlight.advanceTitle: Open-weight and edge-runnable AI that need not phone home
spotlight.advanceSummary: Capable open-weight models (including efficient MoE ‘Flash’ tiers and smaller distilled models) plus mature local runtimes mean useful assistance can run on locked laptops, phones, and mini PCs — offline or air-gapped — if the local workflow, power, and update path exist.
spotlight.encourageCopy: Invent a way this night school can help adults study without sending their words out of the room.

research.topic: Open-weight / small LLMs for local and edge private inference (2026)
bullets: DeepSeek-V4-Flash (preview 2026): open-weight MoE ~284B total / ~13B active, long context, positioned as a fast efficient open tier competitive with much larger closed systems on many tasks.
Broader 2025–2026 wave: quantized small and mid models, on-device runtimes, and edge accelerators make offline chat, tutoring, and drafting newly practical without cloud APIs.
Privacy and control are the product when prompts must not cross a monitored gateway — capability alone does not invent the classroom kit, trust model, or update path.

mission.title: Night school under the filter at North Stack
mission.scene: Omar locks the stairwell door before he powers the secondhand laptop. On North Stack’s third floor, adults wait for exam help the public filter just killed mid-sentence. Last month a rights question flagged a shared cloud account. Three learners stopped coming. They still need the certificate. The only smart tutor still phones pipes someone else can watch.
mission.briefMd:
## The place

Omar locks the stairwell door before he powers the secondhand laptop. The bulb in the North Stack corridor hums. On the third floor of a high-rise block, twelve adults unfold cheap chairs around two folding tables. This is night school — exam prep, job forms, and the plain language of rights that the daytime curriculum skips.

He opens the browser tutor the city library still recommends. The page spins. Then it dies mid-sentence on a history prompt. The public filter won again.

Last month someone typed a careful question about assembly law into a free cloud chatbot on the shared account. The session froze. Two days later a block warden asked why the community room was “studying politics.” Three learners stopped coming. They still need the certificate. They will not risk another flag.

Omar prints worksheets when the toner lasts. He answers what he can from memory. The queue is longer than one volunteer. Learners who can pay for private tutors leave the stack. Everyone else learns to ask smaller questions.

## The bigger problem

The driver is not a lack of curiosity. It is a learning stack that only gets smart by shipping every prompt through pipes someone else can watch, throttle, or stain. Convenience still points at the cloud. Fear teaches silence faster than any lesson plan.

Learning stalls when tools cut out on the exact topics adults need for exams and work. Fear rises when a prompt can become evidence. Burnout hits Omar and the two other volunteers first. When enrollment drops, funders call the program low demand. The demand went underground or went silent.

## Your job

Invent a way this room can give honest help on a bad connectivity night without sending people’s words out of the building. Stakeholder: **Omar, volunteer tutor lead**. He will not deploy a toy that gets someone hurt. He also cannot keep serving twelve adults with worksheets alone.

Name who holds the device keys, how wrong answers get caught, and how a nervous first-time learner starts a session without feeling watched. One room first — not a national network on turn one.

suggestedWhy.ai: Assistance that runs on the school's own laptops, offline, can lift Learning without sending student work away.
